# Daniel 1 — Disagreement Log
**Generated by:** SOPHIA | **Threshold:** <70% word overlap

---

## 1:4 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Youths in-whom [there was] no blemish, and-good-of-appearance, and-skilled in-all wisdom, and-knowing knowledge, and-discerning-of learning, and-in-whom [was] ability to-stand in-the-palace-of the-king; and-to-teach-them the-writing and-the-language-of [the]-Chaldeans. |
| LOGOS | Youths without blemish, of good appearance and skillful in all wisdom, endowed with knowledge, understanding learning, and competent to stand in the king's palace, and to teach them the literature and language of the Chaldeans. |
| PNEUMA | Young men who were healthy, handsome, intelligent, well-educated, quick learners, and qualified to serve in the king's palace. They were to be taught the language and literature of Babylon. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 1:8 (overlap: 0%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-Daniel set upon his-heart that he-would-not-defile-himself with-the-king's-food and-with-the-wine-of his-drinking; and-he-requested from-the-chief-of the-eunuchs that he-would-not-defile-himself. |
| LOGOS | But Daniel resolved that he would not defile himself with the king's food, or with the wine that he drank. Therefore he asked the chief of the eunuchs to allow him not to defile himself. |
| PNEUMA | But Daniel made up his mind not to defile himself by eating the king's food or drinking his wine. He asked the chief of staff for permission to eat other things instead. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 1:13 (overlap: 4%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | Then-let our-appearance be-seen before-you, and-the-appearance-of the-youths who-eat the-king's-food, and-according-to what-you-see, deal with your-servants." |
| LOGOS | Then let our appearance and the appearance of the youths who eat the king's food be observed by you, and deal with your servants according to what you see." |
| PNEUMA | "At the end of ten days, compare us with the young men who eat from the king's table. Then decide what to do with us based on what you see." |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 1:16 (overlap: 6%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-the-steward was carrying-away their-food and-the-wine-of their-drink, and-giving to-them vegetables. |
| LOGOS | So the steward took away their food and the wine they were to drink, and gave them vegetables. |
| PNEUMA | So from then on, the attendant gave them vegetables instead of the rich food and wine. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 1:5 (overlap: 7%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-the-king appointed for-them a-daily-portion from-the-king's-food and-from-the-wine-of his-drinking, and-to-nourish-them three years, and-at-their-end they-would-stand before the-king. |
| LOGOS | The king assigned them a daily portion of the food that the king ate, and of the wine that he drank. They were to be educated for three years, and at the end of that time they were to stand before the king. |
| PNEUMA | The king assigned them a daily serving of the food and wine from his own table. They were to be trained for three years, after which they would enter the king's service. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.

---

## 1:2 (overlap: 7%)

| Translator | Rendering |
|---|---|
| EMET | And-the-Lord gave into-his-hand Jehoiakim king-of Judah, and-a-part-of the-vessels-of the-house-of God; and-he-brought-them to-the-land-of Shinar, to-the-house-of his-god, and-the-vessels he-brought to-the-treasure-house-of his-god. |
| LOGOS | And the Lord gave Jehoiakim king of Judah into his hand, with some of the vessels of the house of God. And he brought them to the land of Shinar, to the house of his god, and placed the vessels in the treasury of his god. |
| PNEUMA | The Lord allowed him to defeat King Jehoiakim and to carry off some of the sacred objects from the Temple of God. He took them to Babylonia and put them in the treasury of his god's temple. |

**SOPHIA ruling:** LOGOS reading adopted for consensus.
